title: CHEMISTRY Paper 01 - General Proficiency
notes: The file you supplied is named 2022, but the paper inside is the May/June 2023 Paper 01 (dated 09 June 2023, footer 01212010/MJ/CSEC 2023), so it is labelled 2023-MJ here.
instructions: This test consists of 60 items. You will have 1 hour and 15 minutes to answer them.
In addition to this test booklet, you should have an answer sheet.
Each item in this test has four suggested answers lettered (A), (B), (C), (D). Read each item you are about to answer and decide which choice is best.

On your answer sheet, find the number which corresponds to your item and shade the space having the same letter as the answer you have chosen. Look at the sample item below. Sample Item: The SI unit of length is the (A) metre (B) second (C) newton (D) kilogram. The best answer to this item is "metre", so (A) has been shaded.
If you want to change your answer, erase it completely before you fill in your new choice.
When you are told to begin, turn the page and work as quickly and as carefully as you can. If you cannot answer an item, go on to the next one. You may return to that item later.
You may do any rough work in this booklet.
Figures are not necessarily drawn to scale.
You may use a silent, non-programmable calculator to answer items.

2023-MJ-D01.alt: Solubility curves. Vertical axis: Mass of crystals that dissolve in 100 g of water (grams), 0 to 120. Horizontal axis: Temperature (°C), 0 to 100. Potassium nitrate rises steeply from about 13 g to over 120 g. Hydrated copper(II) sulfate rises from about 15 g to about 80 g. Sodium chloride is almost flat at about 37 g. Potassium sulfate rises slowly from about 7 g to about 25 g. At 20 °C sodium chloride is the highest curve; potassium nitrate crosses it at about 25 °C.

2023-MJ-D02.alt: Nuclide symbol: X with mass number 40 at top left, atomic number 20 at bottom left and charge 2+ at top right.

2023-MJ-D03A.alt: Option A: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds one cross and one dot; the right circle has six crosses and the left circle has no other electrons.

2023-MJ-D03B.alt: Option B: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds two crosses and two dots (two shared pairs); each circle has four other electrons.

2023-MJ-D03C.alt: Option C: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds three crosses and three dots (three shared pairs); each circle has two other electrons.

2023-MJ-D03D.alt: Option D: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds one cross and one dot (one shared pair); the left circle has six dots and the right circle six crosses.

2023-MJ-D04A.alt: Option A: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). The curve rises steeply from the origin, then levels off to a flat line.

2023-MJ-D04B.alt: Option B: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). The curve starts high and falls, levelling off near the time axis.

2023-MJ-D04C.alt: Option C: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). A straight line falls from high on the volume axis to the time axis.

2023-MJ-D04D.alt: Option D: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). A straight line rises steadily from the origin.

2023-MJ-D05.alt: Reaction sequence: FeCO₃ goes to FeO (stage I), FeO goes to Fe₂O₃ (stage II), Fe₂O₃ goes to Fe₂(SO₄)₃ (stage III), and Fe₂(SO₄)₃ goes to Fe(OH)₃ (stage IV).

2023-MJ-D06A.alt: Option A: displayed formula CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃ (four carbons with the double bond between the second and third carbons).

2023-MJ-D06B.alt: Option B: displayed formula CH₂=CH-CH₂-CH₃ (four carbons with the double bond between the first and second carbons).

2023-MJ-D06C.alt: Option C: displayed formula of propane, CH₃-CH₂-CH₃.

2023-MJ-D06D.alt: Option D: displayed formula of propene, CH₃-CH=CH₂.

2023-MJ-D07.alt: Flow chart with ETHENE in a circle. An arrow labelled H₂O, conc. H₂SO₄ leads to box I; another arrow leads to a box labelled POLYETHENE; a downward arrow labelled Br₂ leads to box II.

2023-MJ-D08.alt: Line graph on grid paper. Vertical axis: Boiling point (°C) from 50 to 250. Horizontal axis: Number of carbon atoms in chain from 1 to 9. A straight line rises from about 65 °C at 1 carbon atom to about 215 °C at 9 carbon atoms; it passes 160 °C at 6 carbon atoms.
